chapters.title: Ch 1 · Security risk management governance and control

sources.title: Past paper · Term unknown · Major Examination

questions.q: According to the Nasdaq report cited in the slides, what percentage of board members at the most vulnerable companies cannot interpret a cybersecurity report?
questions.e: 91% of board members at the most vulnerable companies cannot interpret a cybersecurity report, which shows the executive–IT knowledge gap.

questions.q: Which framework is described as a governance framework used to create business value from IT investments?
questions.e: Val IT focuses on value creation from IT investments; Risk IT covers IT risk; COBIT is the overall IT governance model.

questions.q: Which framework provides an end-to-end, comprehensive view of all risks related to the use of IT?
questions.e: Risk IT gives the end-to-end view of IT-related risk and complements and extends COBIT and Val IT.

questions.q: What is the relationship between Risk IT, COBIT and Val IT?
o: Risk IT replaces COBIT and Val IT
COBIT is a subset of Risk IT
Risk IT complements and extends COBIT and Val IT
questions.e: The slides state that Risk IT complements and extends COBIT and Val IT to make a more complete IT governance resource.

questions.q: Why is it a mistake for an enterprise to try to eliminate all risk?
o: It may eliminate the very risks that drive profit and value creation
questions.e: Enterprises achieve return by taking risks. Eliminating all risk means missing opportunities for value creation.

questions.q: Cybersecurity management includes which two components?
questions.e: The slides define cybersecurity management as including governance and risk management.

questions.q: Which requirement type provides confidence that a security function is performing as expected?
questions.e: Assurance requirements provide confidence that the security function works as expected; functional requirements define its behavior.

questions.q: A company requires every server to use the same approved anti-virus product. This is an example of a:
questions.e: Standards mean adopting common hardware and software mechanisms and products throughout the enterprise, such as anti-virus and firewalls.

questions.q: ISO 17799, Common Criteria and ITIL are given in the slides as examples of:
questions.e: Guidelines are recommendations for implementation, procurement, and planning. The slides list ISO 17799, Common Criteria, and ITIL as examples.

questions.q: Password rules, VPN setup and IDS configuration that set a minimum level of security configuration are examples of:
questions.e: Baselines are benchmarks that ensure a minimum, platform-unique security configuration across systems.

questions.q: Which planning level focuses on very specific actions to react to an incident, fighting fires at the keyboard level?
questions.e: Operational planning is short term and deals with specific reactions to incidents.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT listed in the slides as an example of a functional policy?
questions.e: Functional policies include data classification, C&A, access control, outsourcing, remote access, mail/Internet use, privacy, dissemination, and sharing control. A firewall rule base is a technical configuration, not a functional policy.

questions.q: According to the slides, how do policies gain credibility?
questions.e: Policies gain credibility when top management visibly supports them.

questions.q: Cybersecurity governance is an integral part of overall corporate governance.
questions.e: The slides state that cybersecurity governance is an integral part of corporate governance.

questions.q: The goal of bridging the executive–IT gap is to turn CEOs and CFOs into technologists.
questions.e: The goal is not to turn business leaders into technologists, but for businesses to adapt to the digital landscape.

questions.q: Procedures are step-by-step actions that must be followed to accomplish a task.
questions.e: That is the slide definition of procedures.

questions.q: Guidelines are mandatory rules that every employee must follow exactly.
questions.e: Guidelines are recommendations. Standards, procedures, and baselines are the enforceable elements.

questions.q: Functional requirements of a security solution are selected based on the risk management process.
questions.e: Functional requirements define the control's security behavior and are selected through risk management.

questions.q: Every type of organization has the same security requirements.
questions.e: Each type of organization has differing security requirements, so security must fit its mission.

questions.q: Tactical security planning is long term and focuses on the overall security policy.
questions.e: That describes strategic planning. Tactical planning is medium term (functional plans).

questions.q: Governance should ensure that outsourced IT infrastructure includes service level agreements.
questions.e: Governance ensures IT meets requirements, supports strategy, and includes SLAs if outsourced.

questions.q: The overarching organizational policy is also called management's security ________.
questions.e: The overarching policy is management's security statement.

questions.q: Security ________ provide a structure for organizing requirements and solutions so security is considered holistically.
questions.e: Security blueprints organize requirements and solutions.

questions.q: ________ planning is medium term and focuses on events that affect the whole organization.
questions.e: Tactical planning covers functional plans.

questions.q: The three properties of the cybersecurity triad are confidentiality, integrity and ________.
questions.e: CIA = confidentiality, integrity, availability.

questions.q: Risk and ________ are two sides of the same coin.
questions.e: The slides pair risk with value creation.

questions.q: Explain why cyber risk should be treated as a business priority rather than only an IT issue.
questions.m: Enterprises depend on automation and integration, so cyber risk affects the whole business and must cross IT silos and integrate with existing risk management. Board members often cannot interpret cybersecurity reports (91% at the most vulnerable companies), so the gap between executives and IT must be bridged. Risk and value are linked: managing risk well protects value without missing opportunities.

questions.q: Describe the policy infrastructure, from management's security statement down to enforceable actions.
questions.m: The overarching policy (management's security statement) is shaped by laws, regulations, goals, objectives, and shareholders' interests. It is interpreted into functional policies such as access control or remote access. Functional policies form the foundation for standards, procedures, baselines, and guidelines, which turn objectives into enforceable actions. Policies gain credibility through top management buy-in.

questions.q: Scenario: A hospital adopts the same firewall security settings as a retail shop because it is cheap. Using business-driven security, explain the problem.
questions.m: Business-driven security aligns the security strategy with the organization's own business needs. Each type of organization has differing security requirements: a hospital protects patient data and life-critical availability, unlike a shop. Security must focus on the organization's mission and be cost effective for that mission, not merely cheap.

questions.q: According to NIST SP 800-30, risk is a function of:
o: The likelihood of a threat-source exercising a vulnerability and the resulting impact
The number of vulnerabilities in a system
The number of attackers in a region
questions.e: NIST SP 800-30 defines risk as a function of likelihood of a threat-source exercising a vulnerability and the resulting impact on organizational assets.

questions.q: What is the difference between a threat and an attack?
o: A threat is potential danger; an attack is actual danger
A threat is actual danger; an attack is potential danger
A threat affects hardware; an attack affects software
questions.e: A threat is any potential danger; an attack is any actual danger to information or systems.

questions.q: The amount of risk remaining after countermeasures and safeguards are applied is called:
questions.e: Residual risk is what remains after safeguards are applied.

questions.q: In which risk management step do you start preparing the Risk Register?
questions.e: The Risk Register is started during Step 1 and updated in later steps.

questions.q: Creating DRP, BCP and IRP contingency plans belongs to which risk management step?
questions.e: Step 4, risk control, creates mitigation strategies, preventive plans, and contingency plans such as DRP, BCP, and IRP.

questions.q: The risk score used to evaluate and rank risks is the combination of:
questions.e: Step 3 ranks risks using the risk score: likelihood combined with impact.

questions.q: Which statement about quantitative risk analysis is TRUE?
o: It is fully quantitative only if all elements are quantified
questions.e: Quantitative analysis assigns objective monetary values and is fully quantitative only when every element is quantified. It requires substantial time and staff.

questions.q: Which analysis is scenario oriented and does not assign absolute numeric values to risk components?
questions.e: Qualitative analysis is scenario oriented and uses ranks rather than absolute numbers.

questions.q: In the AS/NZS 4360 matrix, a risk that is 'likely' (B) with a 'major' (4) consequence is rated:
questions.e: Row B, column 4 is E: Extreme risk, requiring immediate action or a decision not to proceed.

questions.q: A company buys cyber insurance to cover losses from a data breach. Which mitigation option is this?
questions.e: Transferring the financial impact to a third party such as an insurer is risk transference.

questions.q: According to the slides, risk acceptance is appropriate when:
o: The cost of the control is higher than the expected loss
questions.e: The slides define risk acceptance as appropriate if the cost is higher than the expected loss.

questions.q: Intrusion detection systems and audit logs that identify security violations are examples of which control type?
questions.e: Detective controls identify and possibly react to security violations.

questions.q: Which countermeasure selection principle corresponds to segregation of duties?
questions.e: Independence of control and subject means the people controlled by a safeguard do not control it, which is segregation of duties.

questions.q: Which of the following is listed as one of the five top qualitative RA techniques?
questions.e: The five techniques are Delphi, SWIFT, decision tree, bow-tie, and probability/consequence matrix.

questions.q: A vulnerability and a hazard are dangerous even when taken separately.
questions.e: The slides say they are not dangerous separately; only when they come together do they become a risk.

questions.q: Vulnerabilities exist in every IT system, product and application.
questions.e: The slide definition of vulnerability states this.

questions.q: Both quantitative and qualitative analysis are often required to get a full picture of risk.
questions.e: Each provides unique capabilities, and both are often needed.

questions.q: Automated risk management tools are always quick to set up.
questions.e: They minimize manual effort and calculate quickly but can be time consuming to set up.

questions.q: Recovery controls restore a system to a normal operating state after integrity or availability is compromised.
questions.e: That is the definition of recovery controls.

questions.q: In the AS/NZS 4360 scale, a Low risk calls for immediate action.
questions.e: Low risk means routine acceptance. Extreme calls for immediate action.

questions.q: Risk avoidance means implementing a countermeasure to reduce the risk impact.
questions.e: That is risk reduction. Avoidance means stopping the activity that creates the risk.

questions.q: Asset value in a cost/benefit analysis should be considered as more than just the cost of the asset.
questions.e: The slides stress that asset value is more than just cost.

questions.q: Any potential danger to information or an information system is a ________.
questions.e: A threat is potential danger; an attack is actual danger.

questions.q: An opportunity for a threat to cause loss is called an ________.
questions.e: Exposure = opportunity for loss.

questions.q: The document used across all five steps to record, rank and track risks is the risk ________.
questions.e: The Risk Register is started in step 1 and used for monitoring in step 5.

questions.q: ________ controls advise employees of the behavior expected of them.
questions.e: Directive (administrative) controls communicate expected behavior.

questions.q: SWIFT analysis stands for Structured ________-If.
questions.e: SWIFT is a Structured What-If technique.

questions.q: A server is worth $10,000 and the exposure factor is 70%. What is the SLE (in dollars)?
Using SLE = $7,000 and ARO = 20, what is the ALE (in dollars)?
ALE before a control is $140,000, ALE after is $50,000 and the annual cost of the control is $30,000. What is the value of the control?
A database worth $50,000 loses 40% of its value per breach, and breaches happen twice a year. What is the ALE?
List and briefly explain the five risk management steps.
questions.m: 1) Identify the risk: find and describe risks and start the Risk Register. 2) Analyze: determine likelihood and impact. 3) Evaluate and rank: compute the risk score and decide whether to accept or treat. 4) Risk control (response planning): plan treatment for top risks, including DRP, BCP, and IRP. 5) Monitor and review: track risks using the Risk Register.

questions.q: Compare quantitative and qualitative risk analysis, including one strength and one weakness of each.
questions.m: Quantitative analysis assigns objective monetary values (SLE, ALE); it gives verifiable, numeric results but is hard to achieve and needs substantial time, data, and people. Qualitative analysis is scenario oriented and ranks threat seriousness and asset sensitivity without absolute numbers; it is quicker but more subjective. Both are often needed for a full picture.

questions.q: Scenario: Laptops are frequently stolen from a branch office. Give one example of each of the four risk mitigation options for this risk.
questions.m: Accept: keep operating without new controls if protection costs more than expected losses. Reduce: install cable locks and full-disk encryption. Transfer: buy insurance or lease laptops from a provider responsible for theft. Avoid: stop issuing laptops at that branch and use fixed desktops instead.

questions.q: An attacker types a DROP TABLE command into a web form input field. This threat is against the:
questions.e: SQL injection is listed under threats against the application.

questions.q: SYN floods and ICMP echo request floods are examples of which network threat?
questions.e: They are denial-of-service threats against the network.

questions.q: Which threat component includes fear of capture, cost of participation and level of technical difficulty?
questions.e: Inhibitors discourage an attack; amplifiers increase it; catalysts trigger it.

questions.q: A university administrator who only needs to change student contact details uses excess update rights to change grades. Which database threat is this?
questions.e: This is the slide example of excessive privilege abuse: privileges exceed job requirements.

questions.q: A CVE entry contains which three items?
questions.e: A CVE entry contains the CVE ID, description, and references.

questions.q: Which threat modeling method focuses on privacy concerns?
questions.e: LINDDUN is the privacy-focused method.

questions.q: In STRIDE, the question 'If an attacker denies doing something, can we prove he did it?' refers to:
questions.e: Repudiation concerns proving that an action was performed.

questions.q: Which method is described as a risk-centric framework with seven stages that brings business objectives and technical requirements together?
questions.e: PASTA (2012) is risk-centric with seven stages and a strategic focus.

questions.q: In an attack tree, child nodes are combined by default using:
questions.e: Child nodes are ORed together by default; special notation indicates AND.

questions.q: The Hybrid Threat Modeling Method (hTMM) combines:
questions.e: hTMM combines SQUARE, Security Cards, and Persona non Grata. Quantitative TMM combines attack trees, STRIDE, and CVSS.

questions.q: OCTAVE focuses on assessing:
o: Organizational risks rather than technological risks
questions.e: OCTAVE is a risk-based strategic method that focuses on organizational risk and does not address technological risk.

questions.q: Which Trike element has four parts (CRUD) in each cell?
questions.e: Trike's actor-asset-action matrix has CRUD parts per cell with associated rules.

questions.q: In the slides' DREAD example, why is cookie theft by eavesdropping prioritized over cookie theft by XSS?
o: Its total score is 13 versus 12, because it needs less skill to exploit
questions.e: Exploitability is 3 for eavesdropping (anyone can run a sniffer) versus 2 for XSS, giving totals of 13 and 12.

questions.q: An organization has no public-facing servers. According to the threat/vulnerability pair concept, the risk from attacks on public-facing servers is:
o: Unknown until a CVSS score is calculated
questions.e: Without the vulnerability, the threat has no path, so the risk in that area is zero.

questions.q: A Trojan horse has two components: one that runs as a server and one that runs as a client.
questions.e: That is how the slides describe Trojan horses.

questions.q: Microsoft still maintains STRIDE as a separate, standalone product.
questions.e: Microsoft no longer maintains STRIDE separately; it is implemented in the SDL Threat Modeling Tool.

questions.q: Emanation vulnerabilities arise from radiation.
questions.e: The slides list emanation vulnerabilities as due to radiation.

questions.q: STRIDE models the in-place system using data-flow diagrams.
questions.e: STRIDE evaluates the system detail design using DFDs.

questions.q: A CVSS score can only be calculated manually and never with an online calculator.
questions.e: A CVSS score can be computed with a calculator available online.

questions.q: Persona non Grata focuses on the motivations and skills of human attackers.
questions.e: PnG examines attacker skills, motivations, and goals.

questions.q: A threat alone, without a vulnerability, is enough to result in a loss.
questions.e: Both the threat and the vulnerability must come together to result in a loss.

questions.q: In Trike, identified threats fall into either elevation of privilege or denial of service.
questions.e: Trike categorizes threats as elevations of privilege or denials of service.

questions.q: ________ spoofing, DNS spoofing and ARP spoofing are forms of spoofing listed in the slides.
questions.e: The slides list IP, DNS, and ARP spoofing.

questions.q: The E in DREAD stands for ________.
questions.e: DREAD = Damage, Reproducibility, Exploitability, Affected users, Discoverability.

questions.q: All vulnerabilities in the ________ have been assigned a CVE identifier.
questions.e: The NVD assigns CVE identifiers to all its vulnerabilities.

questions.q: In an attack tree, the root of the tree is the adversary's ________.
questions.e: The root represents the attacker's goal.

questions.q: OCTAVE stands for Operationally Critical Threat, Asset, and ________ Evaluation.
questions.e: OCTAVE = Operationally Critical Threat, Asset, and Vulnerability Evaluation.

questions.q: Using DREAD, a threat scores D=3, R=3, E=2, A=1, D=2. What is its total score?
Cookie theft by eavesdropping scores D=3, R=2, E=3, A=2, D=3. What is its DREAD total?
questions.e: 3 + 2 + 3 + 2 + 3 = 13, matching the slide example.

questions.q: Explain the six components of a threat and give one example of each.
questions.m: Threat agents are who attacks (criminals, disgruntled employees). Motivators are why (personal gain, politics). Capability is the means (software, training). Catalysts trigger the attack (events, technology changes). Amplifiers increase the likelihood (fame, peer pressure, scripting tools). Inhibitors discourage it (fear of capture, cost, law enforcement).

questions.q: Compare STRIDE and DREAD. How would you use them together?
questions.m: STRIDE classifies threats into Spoofing, Tampering, Repudiation, Information disclosure, Denial of service, and Elevation of privilege, usually by walking a data-flow diagram of the system. DREAD scores each threat on Damage, Reproducibility, Exploitability, Affected users, and Discoverability. Use STRIDE to find and categorize threats, then DREAD to rank them so the highest totals are handled first.

questions.q: Scenario: An attacker wants to read a confidential file on a password-protected PC. Sketch an attack tree in text notation.
questions.m: Goal: Read file from password-protected PC. 1. Get the password: 1.1 search the desk, 1.2 social-engineer the owner. 2. Gain network access. 3. Gain physical access: 3.1 boot with a CD, 3.2 remove the hard disk. Child nodes are ORed by default: any one path achieves the goal.

questions.q: In a well-developed risk management program, which two formal processes are at work?
o: Risk identification and assessment, and risk control
questions.e: The slides name risk identification and assessment, and risk control.

questions.q: Which community of interest is responsible for resource allocation and prioritization of security concerns?
questions.e: Management allocates resources and prioritizes security concerns.

questions.q: Which community of interest plays a crucial role in early detection of threats?
questions.e: Users play a crucial role in early detection and proper response to threats.

questions.q: When creating the asset inventory, assets should be identified:
o: Without pre-judging the value of each asset
questions.e: Identification is done without pre-judging value; values are assigned later.

questions.q: Which of the following is a sample attribute for PEOPLE assets?
questions.e: People attributes include position, supervisor, security clearance, and special skills.

questions.q: Which attribute belongs to DATA assets?
questions.e: Data attributes include classification, owner, size, structure, online/offline, location, and backup procedures.

questions.q: Asset classification categories must be:
questions.e: Categories must be comprehensive and mutually exclusive.

questions.q: Which is NOT listed as a factor in asset valuation?
questions.e: The factors are cost and impact on profitability, revenue, and public image.

questions.q: In a weighted factor analysis, an asset's weighted score is calculated by:
o: Multiplying each criterion score by its weight and summing
questions.e: Weighted score = Σ (criterion score × weight).

questions.q: After assets are ranked, what is the outcome of threat identification?
questions.e: The outcome is a threat–vulnerability matrix, with threats prioritized per asset.

questions.q: An email server with anti-virus software that is not updated faces a virus attack. The vulnerability here is:
questions.e: Asset = email server; vulnerability = anti-virus not updated; threat = virus attack.

questions.q: The TVA worksheet combines:
o: The prioritized list of assets and vulnerabilities with the prioritized list of threats
questions.e: It combines the asset/vulnerability list and the threat list into one Threat–Vulnerability–Asset worksheet.

questions.q: Managing risk is one of the key responsibilities of every manager in the organization.
questions.e: The slides state this directly.

questions.q: The IT community of interest takes the leadership role in addressing risk.
questions.e: Cyber security takes the leadership role; IT builds and maintains secure systems.

questions.q: People and procedures are considered information assets in the inventory.
questions.e: Assets include people, procedures, data, software, hardware, and networking elements.

questions.q: Personnel may require an alternative classification scheme.
questions.e: Some asset types, such as personnel, may require an alternative scheme.

questions.q: Asset valuation assigns relative values so that the most valuable assets get the highest priority.
questions.e: Comparative judgments ensure the most valuable assets are prioritized.

questions.q: Risk assessment happens before asset identification in the lifecycle.
questions.e: Assets are identified, classified, valued, and ranked first; risk assessment comes after the TVA worksheet.

questions.q: An incorrect router configuration that could cause loss of connectivity is an example of a vulnerability.
questions.e: The slides give incorrect router configuration as the vulnerability for the router asset.

questions.q: A network asset tracker is a tool that can support asset inventory.
questions.e: Network asset tracker and asset management tools are listed.

questions.q: TVA stands for Threat, Vulnerability, ________.
questions.e: TVA = Threat–Vulnerability–Asset.

questions.q: The ________ community of interest builds and maintains secure systems.
questions.e: IT builds and maintains secure systems.

questions.q: Evaluating risk controls uses the ________ model to decide which options are cost-effective.
questions.e: The CBA model determines cost-effective controls.

questions.q: A classification scheme categorizes assets based on their sensitivity and security ________.
questions.e: Classification is based on sensitivity and security needs.

questions.q: After identifying and valuing assets, the next step is asset ________: prioritizing according to value.
questions.e: Asset ranking prioritizes by value.

questions.q: Weights: revenue 40, profitability 35, public image 25. An asset scores 0.5, 0.8 and 1.0. What is its weighted score?
Weights: revenue 30, profitability 40, public image 30. Asset A scores 0.9, 0.7, 0.4; Asset B scores 0.6, 0.9, 0.8. Which asset ranks higher, A or B?
Describe the steps from asset identification to the TVA worksheet.
questions.m: First build an asset inventory of people, procedures, data, software, hardware, and networking, tracking relevant attributes without pre-judging value. Classify assets by sensitivity with comprehensive, mutually exclusive categories. Value assets using factors such as cost, revenue, profitability, and public image (weighted factor analysis), then rank them. Identify threats and vulnerabilities per asset to form a threat–vulnerability matrix. Combine the prioritized lists into the TVA worksheet, which feeds risk assessment.

questions.q: Explain why different communities of interest must work together in risk management.
questions.m: No single group can manage risk alone. Cyber security leads the effort and sets direction; IT builds and maintains secure systems; management provides resources and decides priorities; users are often first to notice threats and must respond properly. Without cooperation, controls are underfunded, poorly implemented, or bypassed.

questions.q: Scenario: A company lists its assets as 'servers', 'laptops', 'computers' and 'customer data'. Critique this classification.
questions.m: The categories are not mutually exclusive: laptops and servers are also computers, so an asset could fall into two categories. They are not comprehensive either: people, procedures, software, and networking elements are missing. A better scheme classifies by sensitivity and security needs (e.g. sensitive, confidential, private, public for data) with every asset fitting exactly one category.

questions.q: Risk assessment is performed primarily to:
questions.e: RA is performed to identify the most serious risks.

questions.q: Which statement describes quantitative risk assessment?
o: Subjective, based on expert opinion, completed quickly
Objective, uses dollar values, requires a lot of data
questions.e: Quantitative RA is objective, uses actual dollar values and formulas, and requires a significant amount of data.

questions.q: Why should the RA team not be the same people responsible for correcting deficiencies?
o: To avoid a conflict of interest
questions.e: Separating the RA team from those who fix deficiencies avoids a conflict of interest, though their input is still important.

questions.q: Which RA component identifies the boundary of what is and is not included?
questions.e: Scope identifies the RA boundary and keeps the RA on track.

questions.q: An incident happened once a month last year. Assuming nothing changes, what is the ARO?
questions.e: Monthly = 12 times per year.

questions.q: Which term refers to the cost of a control?
questions.e: Safeguard value is the cost of a control, e.g. $50 × 100 computers = $5,000.

questions.q: Which is a LIMITATION of quantitative risk assessment?
o: It relies only on expert opinion
questions.e: Limitations: accurate data isn't always available, and it's hard to ensure controls are used as expected.

questions.q: In qualitative RA, impact is defined as:
o: The negative result if a risk occurs
The likelihood a threat exploits a vulnerability
questions.e: Impact is the negative result if a risk occurs; probability is the likelihood.

questions.q: In the risk determination formula, why is a likelihood of zero never used?
o: Vulnerabilities with zero likelihood are removed from the asset/vulnerability list
questions.e: Vulnerabilities with zero likelihood are removed from the list, so zero is not used.

questions.q: If assumptions and data are 80% accurate, the element of uncertainty is:
questions.e: Uncertainty = 1 − 0.8 = 20%.

questions.q: Which deliverable assigns a ranked risk rating for each uncontrolled asset–vulnerability pair?
questions.e: The ranked vulnerability risk worksheet rates each uncontrolled asset–vulnerability pair.

questions.q: When should an RA be conducted after a control is implemented?
o: To ensure the control's suitability and functionality
questions.e: After implementation, an RA ensures the control's suitability and functionality.

questions.q: Risk assessment is a one-time activity performed only at project initiation.
questions.e: RA is a continuous process conducted at several points.

questions.q: A qualitative risk assessment can be completed rather quickly.
questions.e: Because it relies on expert opinion, it can be completed quickly.

questions.q: SLE includes the value of hardware, software and data.
questions.e: The slides say SLE includes hardware, software, and data.

questions.q: Quantitative risk assessment can be automated, for example with an Excel sheet.
questions.e: Automation is listed as a benefit.

questions.q: Likelihood can be expressed as a number between 0.1 and 1.0 or between 1 and 100.
questions.e: Both scales are given in the slides.

questions.q: In the risk determination formula, the percentage of risk already controlled is added to the risk.
questions.e: It is subtracted; the element of uncertainty is added.

questions.q: The ranked risk worksheet is the initial working document for assessing and controlling risk.
questions.e: It feeds the next step in the risk management process.

questions.q: Critical areas help the RA team focus only on what is important.
questions.e: Identifying critical areas keeps the team focused.

questions.q: ALE is calculated by multiplying SLE by ________.
questions.e: ALE = SLE × ARO.

questions.q: ________ is the likelihood that a threat will exploit a vulnerability.
questions.e: Probability (likelihood) is one of the two qualitative dimensions.

questions.q: The three critical components of a risk assessment are scope, critical areas and ________.
questions.e: Scope, critical areas, and team.

questions.q: Risk level in qualitative assessment = Probability × ________.
questions.e: Risk level = probability × impact.

questions.q: The ________ criteria analysis worksheet assigns a ranked value or impact weight to each information asset.
questions.e: The weighted criteria analysis worksheet ranks asset values.

questions.q: SLE is $5,000 and ARO is 12. What is the ALE (in dollars)?
Laptops are worth $2,000 and one is stolen each quarter. What is the ALE?
ALE before = $8,000, ALE after = $2,000, control cost = $1,000. What are the savings with the control?
Asset value 50, likelihood 1.0, no controls, data 90% accurate. Using the risk determination formula, what is the risk?
Asset value 100, likelihood 0.5, 50% already controlled, data 80% accurate. What is the risk?
questions.e: Base 50; −25 (50% controlled) + 10 (20% uncertainty) = 35.

questions.q: Asset value 80, likelihood 0.5, 25% already controlled, data 90% accurate. What is the risk?
Compare quantitative and qualitative risk assessment, including one benefit and one limitation of each.
questions.m: Quantitative RA is objective: it uses actual dollar values and formulas (SLE, ARO, ALE). Its results are accurate, verifiable, and automatable, but it needs large amounts of data that aren't always available. Qualitative RA is subjective: experts rate probability and impact with words or percentages. It is quick to complete but depends on expert opinion and is less precise.

questions.q: A company loses about 6 USB drives a year, each costing $500 including data. Encryption software costing $1,200 a year would cut losses to 2 drives a year. Should they buy it? Show your working.
questions.m: SLE = $500. ALE before = 500 × 6 = $3,000. ALE after = 500 × 2 = $1,000. Savings = 3,000 − 1,000 − 1,200 = $800. Savings are positive, so buying the encryption software is justified.

questions.q: Explain the three critical components of a risk assessment and why each matters.
questions.m: Scope defines the boundary of the RA (what is and isn't included) and keeps it on track. Critical areas identify the important parts inside the scope, such as a web server's single point of failure, so the team focuses on what matters. The team should not be the people responsible for fixing deficiencies, avoiding a conflict of interest, although their input is valuable.

questions.q: Which is NOT one of the three preliminary actions before performing an RA?
questions.e: The three preliminary actions are defining the assessment, reviewing previous findings, and identifying the management structure.

questions.q: A short sentence describing what a system does, without much detail, is the system's:
questions.e: The mission is a short, easy-to-define statement of what the system does.

questions.q: Asking 'Do you have documentation of the current configuration?' helps define the system's:
questions.e: These questions gather operational characteristics: how the system operates in your environment.

questions.q: Unapproved recommendations from a previous RA give insight into:
o: The level of residual risk and the organization's receptiveness to the control
questions.e: Unapproved recommendations show the accepted residual risk and receptiveness to controls.

questions.q: Why should the RA scope be kept within the ownership of a single entity?
o: So recommendations have one clear decision maker and don't cross management lines
Because PING only works on one network
questions.e: Matching the RA to the management structure avoids crossing management lines.

questions.q: Evaluating assets outside the boundary of the RA is called:
questions.e: Scope creep wastes time and resources.

questions.q: A web server earning $10,000 per hour is down for 2 hours while its hard drive is replaced. The $20,000 of lost revenue belongs to its:
questions.e: Recovery value includes the cost of getting the asset operational, including downtime.

questions.q: Which technique identifies the running operating system of a target?
questions.e: Fingerprinting identifies the OS; WHOIS finds domain names; PING finds IP addresses.

questions.q: An exploit assessment is performed through:
questions.e: Exploit assessment = penetration testing.

questions.q: Controls that have a specified implementation date are called:
questions.e: Planned controls have a specified implementation date.

questions.q: What happens in Phase TWO of presenting the risk assessment results?
o: The ranked risk list is submitted to top management
A POAM is prepared to implement approved items within budget and time
questions.e: Phase one submits ranked risks for approval; phase two builds the POAM.

questions.q: Which is the FIRST step of the eight-step RA plan?
o: Identify assets and activities to address
questions.e: The plan begins by identifying assets and activities to address.

questions.q: A risk assessment is a one-day project.
questions.e: RA is not a one-day project; it is a continuous process that takes time and planning.

questions.q: The mission of a system is harder to define than its operational characteristics.
questions.e: Compared to operational characteristics, the mission is easy to define.

questions.q: Organizations with high employee turnover tend to have more cybersecurity issues.
questions.e: The slides say high-turnover organizations have higher cybersecurity issues.

questions.q: Hot, warm and cold sites are forms of redundancy considered when valuing facilities.
questions.e: Facilities and supplies include insurance and redundancy (hot, warm, cold sites).

questions.q: NMAP, NESSUS, SATAN and SAINT are tools used to capture data in a vulnerability assessment.
questions.e: They are listed as data-capture tools.

questions.q: Controls fall into three primary categories: administrative, technical and physical.
questions.e: Those are the three control categories in the slides.

questions.q: Mitigating recommendations should include an estimate of operational impact.
questions.e: Recommendations include cost and time estimates, operational impact, and CBA.

questions.q: Reviewing past audits is unnecessary if a new RA is being performed.
questions.e: Reviewing past audits and past RAs is a listed best practice.

questions.q: POAM stands for Plan Of ________ and Milestones.
questions.e: POAM = Plan Of Actions and Milestones.

questions.q: ________ value is the cost to purchase a new asset in place of the old one.
questions.e: Replacement value buys a new asset.

questions.q: The ________ tool is used to identify domain names during information gathering.
questions.e: WHOIS identifies domain names.

questions.q: Before assessing, decide whether you will assess a system or a ________.
questions.e: The assessment can target a system or a process.

questions.q: Threats can be identified by reviewing historical data or by threat ________.
questions.e: The two methods are historical data and threat modeling.

questions.q: A database server earns $5,000 per hour. A failure needs a $800 disk and 3 hours of downtime. What is the recovery value?
questions.e: Downtime 3 × 5,000 = 15,000 plus the 800 disk = 15,800.

questions.q: A web server generating $10,000 per hour needs 2 hours to repair. How much lost revenue is included in the recovery value?
questions.e: 2 × 10,000 = 20,000, as in the slide example.

questions.q: Describe the three preliminary actions before performing a risk assessment.
questions.m: 1) Define the assessment: decide whether a system or process is assessed and describe it as it currently is, covering operational characteristics (how it operates, diagrams, configuration documents) and its mission (a short statement of what it does). 2) Review previous findings: use earlier reports' assets, threats, vulnerabilities, recommendations, the status of accepted recommendations, and unapproved ones. 3) Identify the management structure: how responsibilities are assigned, keeping the scope within a single owner.

questions.q: Explain the difference between replacement value and recovery value with an example of each.
questions.m: Replacement value is the cost to purchase a new asset in place of the old one, e.g. $1,500 to buy a new laptop after one is stolen. Recovery value is the cost to get an existing asset operational after a failure, including repair and downtime, e.g. replacing a web server's hard drive, reinstalling the OS, restoring backups, and adding $20,000 of revenue lost during a 2-hour outage at $10,000 per hour.

questions.q: Scenario: You finished a risk assessment of the company's web servers. Explain how you would present the results to management.
questions.m: Present results in two phases. Phase one: submit the list of ranked risks, with mitigating recommendations based on threat/vulnerability pairs, cost and time estimates, operational impact, and cost-benefit analysis, to top management for approval. Phase two: for the approved items, prepare a POAM (Plan Of Actions and Milestones) showing how and when they will be implemented within the given budget and time, and track results against it.

questions.q: Which pair of frameworks does Risk IT complement and extend?
questions.e: Risk IT complements and extends COBIT and Val IT.

questions.q: A board of directors approves the organization's long-range security policy. This is which level of planning?
questions.e: Strategic planning is long term and high level, e.g. the overall security policy.

questions.q: Which element turns functional policies into enforceable actions by specifying the minimum security configuration for a platform?
questions.e: Baselines ensure a minimum, platform-unique security configuration.

questions.q: Which requirement type is selected based on the risk management process and defines the security behavior of a control?
questions.e: Functional requirements define security behavior and are chosen through risk management.

questions.q: A disgruntled former employee who could harm the company, but has not yet acted, is best described as a:
questions.e: A threat agent has the potential to cause a threat; an attacker is the actual cause of an attack.

questions.q: Which risk management step uses the Risk Register to monitor, track and review risks?
questions.e: Step 5, monitor and review, uses the Risk Register.

questions.q: In the AS/NZS 4360 matrix, a 'rare' (E) likelihood with an 'insignificant' (1) consequence is:
questions.e: Row E, column 1 is L: routine acceptance.

questions.q: A company stops offering an online service because its risk is too high. Which mitigation option is this?
questions.e: Stopping the activity that creates the risk is avoidance.

questions.q: Restoring data from backup after a ransomware incident is an example of which control type?
questions.e: Recovery controls restore systems to normal operation.

questions.q: Which countermeasure selection principle requires that a safeguard can be tested and audited?
questions.e: Audit capability means the safeguard can be tested and audited.

questions.q: Val IT provides an end-to-end view of all IT-related risks.
questions.e: That describes Risk IT. Val IT creates business value from IT investments.

questions.q: Cybersecurity management includes governance and risk management.
questions.e: Both are listed as parts of cybersecurity management.

questions.q: Procedures are recommendations that employees may choose to follow.
questions.e: Procedures are step-by-step actions that must be followed; guidelines are recommendations.

questions.q: Risk management should identify potential risks before they occur and across the life of the project.
questions.e: That is the stated purpose of risk management.

questions.q: Qualitative risk analysis assigns absolute monetary values to all risk components.
questions.e: Qualitative analysis does not assign absolute numeric values; quantitative does.

questions.q: Corrective controls react to a detected incident to reduce the chance of it recurring.
questions.e: That is the definition of corrective controls.

questions.q: The three properties protected by cybersecurity are confidentiality, integrity and ________.
questions.e: CIA triad.

questions.q: Policies gain credibility through top ________ buy-in.
questions.e: Top management buy-in gives policies credibility.

questions.q: Risk remaining after countermeasures are applied is ________ risk.
questions.e: Residual risk.

questions.q: The Delphi technique and bow-tie analysis are ________ risk analysis techniques.
questions.e: Both are among the five top qualitative techniques.

questions.q: An asset worth $20,000 has an exposure factor of 25%. What is the SLE?
SLE = $5,000 and the threat occurs 6 times a year. What is the ALE?
ALE before = $30,000, ALE after = $10,000, annual control cost = $12,000. What is the value of the control?
questions.e: 30,000 − 10,000 − 12,000 = 8,000, so the control is worth buying.

questions.q: Explain the difference between standards, procedures, guidelines and baselines, with one example of each.
questions.m: Standards adopt common hardware and software mechanisms enterprise-wide (e.g. one approved anti-virus). Procedures are step-by-step actions that must be followed (e.g. how to reset a password). Guidelines are recommendations for implementation and planning (e.g. ISO 17799, ITIL). Baselines are benchmarks setting a minimum, platform-unique security configuration (e.g. password rules, VPN setup).

questions.q: Scenario: A hospital's patient records server faces ransomware. Describe how the five types of security controls could each be applied.
questions.m: Directive: an acceptable-use policy and awareness training telling staff not to open suspicious attachments. Preventive: email filtering, patching, and access controls. Detective: an IDS or anti-malware alerts that spot encryption activity. Corrective: isolating infected machines and removing the malware so it doesn't recur. Recovery: restoring patient records from clean backups to return to normal operations.

questions.q: According to Chapter 1, cybersecurity governance must be fully integrated into:
questions.e: Governance is fully integrated into overall risk analysis/management.

questions.q: Which is an example of a functional policy?
questions.e: Remote access is one of the functional policies listed.

questions.q: The formula 'Value of control = ALE(before) − ALE(after) − ACS' is used to:
o: Decide whether a control is cost-justified
questions.e: A positive value means the control saves more than it costs.

questions.q: Which qualitative technique is known as a 'Structured What-If'?
questions.e: SWIFT = Structured What-If Technique.

questions.q: Using a stolen session ID cookie to access someone else's session is:
questions.e: Session hijacking uses a stolen session ID.

questions.q: Which threat modeling method combines attack trees, STRIDE and CVSS?
questions.e: Quantitative TMM applies attack trees, STRIDE, and CVSS in synergy.

questions.q: In LINDDUN, being able to identify the sender of an email within a group is:
questions.e: Identifiability is identifying the subject within a set of subjects.

questions.q: Which Chapter 4 community of interest is responsible for building and maintaining secure systems?
questions.e: IT builds and maintains secure systems.

questions.q: A worksheet listing assets by priority on one axis and threats by priority on the other, recording vulnerabilities in the cells, is the:
questions.e: The Threat–Vulnerability–Asset worksheet combines both prioritized lists.

questions.q: Which asset attribute is tracked for procedures?
o: Where it is stored for update purposes
questions.e: Procedure attributes include description, purpose, related elements, and storage locations for reference and update.

questions.q: A qualitative risk assessment is described as:
o: Subjective and based on expert opinion
questions.e: Qualitative RA is subjective and relies on experts; it is quick.

questions.q: In the risk determination formula, if data is 70% accurate, the uncertainty used is:
questions.e: Uncertainty = 1 − 0.7 = 30%.

questions.q: A web server's critical area in the RA scope example was:
o: Only data exchanged with the database
Single point of failure and OS patch status
questions.e: Web server: SPOF and OS updates; database: exchanged data; firewall: traffic inspection.

questions.q: During RA preparation, which information comes from reviewing the current status of ACCEPTED recommendations?
o: The organization's receptiveness to rejected controls
The effectiveness of recommendations in place and justification for those not in place
questions.e: Accepted recommendations show effectiveness (in place) and justification (not in place).

questions.q: Which is the correct order of the last four steps of the RA plan?
o: Assess threats/vulnerabilities/exploits, evaluate risks, develop recommendations, present to management
Evaluate risks, assess exploits, present, recommend
Identify countermeasures, identify assets, present, evaluate
questions.e: Steps 5–8: assess, evaluate risks, develop recommendations, present recommendations.

questions.q: Port scanning and trace routing to detect network topology are threats against the:
questions.e: They are information-gathering threats against the network.

questions.q: Security blueprints are used to identify and design security requirements.
questions.e: That is one purpose of security blueprints.

questions.q: Both quantitative and qualitative risk analysis are often required to get a full picture.
questions.e: Each has unique capabilities.

questions.q: OCTAVE addresses technological risks rather than organizational risks.
questions.e: OCTAVE focuses on organizational risks and does not address technological risks.

questions.q: In attack trees, special notation is needed to show AND relationships.
questions.e: Children are ORed by default; AND needs special notation.

questions.q: Asset values are assigned during asset identification, before the inventory is complete.
questions.e: Assets are identified without pre-judging value; values come later.

questions.q: A likelihood value of zero is used for vulnerabilities that are very unlikely.
questions.e: Zero is not used; zero-likelihood vulnerabilities are removed.

questions.q: Scope creep wastes time and resources by evaluating assets outside the RA boundary.
questions.e: That is the definition in Chapter 6.

questions.q: The POAM is submitted in phase one for top management to approve the ranked risks.
questions.e: Phase one submits the ranked risk list; the POAM is phase two.

questions.q: ________ IT is a governance framework used to create business value from IT investments.
questions.e: Val IT.

questions.q: The step of risk management that creates DRP, BCP and IRP plans is risk ________.
questions.e: Step 4: risk control (risk response planning).

questions.q: The D in STRIDE stands for denial of ________.
questions.e: STRIDE: Denial of service.

questions.q: Asset classification categories must be comprehensive and mutually ________.
questions.e: Comprehensive and mutually exclusive.

questions.q: The ________ risk worksheet is the final summary of the risk assessment.
questions.e: The ranked (vulnerability) risk worksheet.

questions.q: Penetration testing is used in an ________ assessment.
questions.e: Exploit assessment = penetration testing.

questions.q: A laptop worth $1,800 is stolen twice a year. Locks costing $400 a year would reduce thefts to once a year. What are the annual savings with the locks?
Asset value 60, likelihood 0.5, 20% already controlled, data 90% accurate. Using the risk determination formula, what is the risk?
A threat scores Damage 2, Reproducibility 3, Exploitability 3, Affected users 2, Discoverability 1. What is the DREAD total?
Weights: cost 20, revenue 50, public image 30. An asset scores 0.5, 0.6 and 0.9. What is its weighted score?
A payment server earns $4,000 per hour. Recovery needs a $1,000 part and 5 hours of downtime. What is the recovery value?
Trace a complete risk management effort from asset identification to presenting results, naming the key deliverable at each stage.
questions.m: Identify assets (asset inventory) without pre-judging value, classify them (asset classification worksheet), and value and rank them (weighted criteria analysis worksheet). Identify threats and vulnerabilities per asset to build the threat–vulnerability matrix and the TVA worksheet. Perform a quantitative (SLE, ARO, ALE) or qualitative (probability × impact) risk assessment and summarize it in the ranked vulnerability risk worksheet. Develop mitigating recommendations with cost-benefit analysis, present the ranked risks to top management, and implement approved items through a POAM.

questions.q: Scenario: An online store's customer database is worth $200,000. A breach would expose 30% of its value and happens about once every two years. A database activity monitoring tool costs $12,000 a year and would cut the rate to once every ten years. Should the store buy it? Show SLE, ARO, ALE and savings.
questions.m: SLE = 200,000 × 0.30 = $60,000. ARO before = 0.5, so ALE before = $30,000. ARO after = 0.1, so ALE after = $6,000. Savings = 30,000 − 6,000 − 12,000 = $12,000. The savings are positive, so the tool is cost-justified.

questions.q: Using STRIDE, identify one threat in each category for an online banking login page and suggest a control for two of them.
questions.m: Spoofing: an attacker logs in with stolen credentials (control: multi-factor authentication). Tampering: changing transfer amounts in transit (control: TLS and integrity checks). Repudiation: a user denies making a transfer (audit logging). Information disclosure: error messages reveal account data. Denial of service: flooding the login page. Elevation of privilege: a normal user gains admin functions.

questions.q: Explain why the risk assessment team should be independent, and how the scope should relate to the management structure.
questions.m: The RA team should not be the people responsible for correcting deficiencies, to avoid a conflict of interest, although their input is important. The scope should be kept within the ownership of a single entity and not cross management lines, so every recommendation has one clear decision maker and the RA can be acted on.

questions.q: If different user groups with different security access levels need to access the same information, which of the following actions should management take?
o: Require specific written approval each time an individual needs to access the information.
Increase the security controls on the information.
Decrease the security level on the information to ensure accessibility and usability of the information.
Decrease the classification label on the information.
questions.e: Raise the controls, never lower the classification. Weakening the label or the security level to make sharing easier exposes the information to everyone below that level; written approval for every access is unworkable.

questions.q: The security functionality defines the expected activities of a security mechanism, and assurance defines:
o: The confidence of the security the mechanism is providing.
The data classification after the security mechanism has been implemented.
The controls the security mechanism will enforce.
questions.e: Functionality is what the mechanism does; assurance is how much confidence you have that it does it correctly and consistently.

questions.q: Which of the following is not a management role in the process of implementing and maintaining security?
questions.e: Management supports the programme, sets its purpose and scope, and delegates responsibility. Carrying out the risk analysis itself is the security team's work, not a management role.

questions.q: What are security policies?
o: Step-by-step directions on how to accomplish security tasks.
Broad, high-level statements from the management.
Detailed documents explaining how security incidents should be handled.
General guidelines used to accomplish a specific security level.
questions.e: Policies are broad, high-level management statements of intent. Step-by-step directions are procedures, and general recommendations are guidelines.

questions.q: Who has the primary responsibility of determining the classification level for information?
questions.e: The data owner classifies the information. Custodians protect it at that level and users follow the handling rules.

questions.q: Which factor is the most important item when it comes to ensuring security is successful in an organization?
o: Updated and relevant security policies and procedures
questions.e: Without senior management support there is no budget, no authority and no enforcement, so awareness, controls and policies never take hold.

questions.q: Which is the best framework that helps organizations meet business challenges in regulatory compliance, risk management and aligning IT strategy with organisational goals?
questions.e: COBIT is the IT governance model covering compliance, risk and alignment of IT with business goals; Risk IT covers IT risk only and Val IT covers value from IT investments. Note: the marker's key on your paper points to Risk IT, so check this one with your instructor.

questions.q: Who should measure the effectiveness of Information System security related controls in an organization?
questions.e: Measuring control effectiveness needs independence from the people who run the controls, which is the systems auditor's role.

questions.q: What would BEST define risk management?
o: The process of assessing the risks
The process of eliminating the risk
The process of reducing risk to an acceptable level
questions.e: Risk can never be eliminated. Risk management reduces it to a level the organization accepts; transfer and assessment are only parts of that process.

questions.q: Making sure that only those who are supposed to access the data can access it is which of the following?
questions.e: Confidentiality restricts access to authorised people. Integrity is about accuracy, availability is about access when needed.

questions.q: Who should be involved in Security Risk Management activities? Choose the best answer.
questions.e: Risk management needs as many perspectives as is practical: each group sees risks the others miss. Clients are stakeholders too, so excluding them loses information.

questions.q: When should risk identification be performed? (select the best answer)
o: Risk identification should be performed on a regular basis throughout the project
questions.e: Identification starts early but is repeated throughout: new risks appear as the project changes, so a one-off pass at the concept phase is not enough.

questions.q: An example of risk mitigation is:
o: Using proven technology in the development of a product to lessen the probability that the product will not work
Accepting a lower profit if costs overrun
Eliminating the cause of a risk
questions.e: Mitigation (reduction) lowers the probability or impact while still doing the activity. Accepting lower profit is acceptance, and eliminating the cause is avoidance.

questions.q: A process that is not part of Security Risk Management is:
questions.e: Security maintenance is an operational activity. Risk management covers identification, policy and the monitoring and control of risks.

questions.q: How is an "attack" represented?
questions.e: An attack needs someone who wants something (motive), a way to do it (method) and a weakness to use (vulnerability). Asset + threat + vulnerability is how risk is represented, not an attack.

questions.q: List 2 types of Cybersecurity Framework and explain. [0.5 Marks]
questions.m: Any two of the ISACA frameworks, explained. Risk IT: an end-to-end view of all risks arising from the use of IT, covering how to be aware of risks and manage them before, during and after they happen. Val IT: a governance framework for creating business value from IT investments. COBIT: the IT governance model that helps deliver value from IT and understand and manage the risks that come with it.

questions.q: Why do executives and IT/security need to have knowledge connections and good relations and communication between both parties? [0.5 Marks]
questions.m: Cyber risk is a business risk, so it cannot be managed inside an IT silo. Executives control budget and priorities but often cannot interpret a security report, while IT understands the risks but not the business goals. Bridging that gap lets risks be expressed in business terms, funded appropriately, and aligned with the organization's objectives, so security supports value creation instead of blocking it.

questions.q: Renee is designing the short-term security plan for her organization and has a one- to six-month planning horizon. What type of plan is she developing? [0.5 Marks]
questions.m: An operational plan. The three levels of security planning are strategic (long range, around five years), tactical (mid term, about one year) and operational (short term, roughly one to six months, covering day-to-day tasks).

questions.q: Explain in detail how a "risk" is represented. [1 Mark]
questions.m: Risk is the possibility that a threat exploits a vulnerability in an asset and causes loss or damage. It is represented as Threat x Vulnerability x Asset value, so risk exists only when all three are present: something valuable, a weakness in it, and someone or something able to exploit that weakness. Its size is judged by the probability of that happening and the impact if it does.

questions.q: What does "residual risk" mean?
o: The security risk that remains after controls have been implemented
Weakness of an asset which can be exploited by a threat
Risk that remains after risk assessment has been performed
A security risk intrinsic to an asset being audited, where no mitigation has taken place
questions.e: Residual risk is what is left after the controls are in place. The weakness itself is a vulnerability, and the risk before any mitigation is inherent risk.

questions.q: This category of control can include the logical mechanisms used to control access and authenticate users.
questions.e: Technical (logical) controls are implemented in software and hardware: authentication, access control lists, encryption. Administrative controls are policies and procedures; physical controls are locks and guards.

questions.q: Which of the following formulas represents total risk?
o: Risk X Vulnerability X Asset value = Total risk
Threat X Vulnerability X Asset value = Total risk
questions.e: Total risk = Threat x Vulnerability x Asset value. Residual risk is that total minus the effect of the controls in place.

questions.q: Which best describes a quantitative risk analysis?
o: A scenario-based analysis to research different security threats
A method used to apply severity levels to potential loss, probability of loss, and risks
A method that assigns monetary values to components in the risk assessment
A method that is based on gut feelings and opinions
questions.e: Quantitative analysis puts money values on assets, losses and controls (SLE, ARO, ALE). Applying severity levels or scenarios without numbers is qualitative.

questions.q: When is it acceptable to not take action on an identified risk?
o: Never. Good security addresses and reduces all risks.
When political issues prevent this type of risk from being addressed.
When the necessary countermeasure is complex.
When the cost of the countermeasure outweighs the value of the asset and potential loss.
questions.e: Accepting a risk is justified when the control costs more than the loss it prevents. Complexity or politics are not valid reasons, and no organization can remove every risk.

questions.q: SQL Injection is a ________ type of threat.
questions.e: SQL injection abuses input handling in the application itself, so it is an application-level threat.

questions.q: An internal IS auditor recommends that incoming accounts payable payment files be encrypted. Which type of control is the auditor recommending?
questions.e: Encryption stops disclosure before it happens, so it is preventive. Detective controls find incidents, corrective controls fix them and directive controls instruct people.

questions.q: Which of the following is not a type of threat?
questions.e: Threats are classified against the network, the host and the application. Management is a category of control, not a threat.

questions.q: What is the prime directive of Risk Management?
o: Reduce all risks regardless of cost
Reduce the risk to a tolerable level
Transfer any risk to external third parties
Prosecute any employees that are violating published security policies
questions.e: The aim is to bring risk down to a tolerable (acceptable) level at a sensible cost, not to remove every risk.

questions.q: If different user groups with different security access levels need to access the same information, which of the following actions should management take?
o: Decrease the security level on the information to ensure accessibility and usability of the information.
Require specific written approval each time an individual needs to access the information.
Increase the security controls on the information.
Decrease the classification label on the information.
questions.e: Strengthen the controls so the information can be shared safely. Lowering the level or the label exposes it, and per-access written approval does not scale.

questions.q: Company X sells laptops online and makes an average profit of $20,000 per week. A typical DoS attack lowers sales by 40%. What is the SLE? [part of 3.5 Marks]
questions.e: SLE = asset value x exposure factor = 20,000 x 0.40 = $8,000 lost per attack.

questions.q: Company X suffers four DoS attacks on average every 6 months. What is the ARO (attacks per year)?
questions.e: ARO is per year: 4 attacks per 6 months = 8 attacks per year.

questions.q: Using SLE = $8,000 and ARO = 8, what is the ALE before the countermeasure?
questions.e: ALE = SLE x ARO = 8,000 x 8 = $64,000 per year.

questions.q: The mitigation service reduces the attacks to 80% of the original number. What is the ALE after the countermeasure?
questions.e: ARO after = 8 x 0.8 = 6.4, so ALE after = 8,000 x 6.4 = $51,200. Note the wording: the marked key treats "reduced 80%" as reduced to 80% of the attacks. If it meant reduced by 80%, ARO would be 1.6 and ALE after $12,800.

questions.q: The service costs $1,000 per month plus $1,500 one-time installation. What is the value of the control (cost benefit analysis) for the first year?
questions.e: Annual cost = 1,000 x 12 + 1,500 = $13,500. Value = ALE before - ALE after - cost = 64,000 - 51,200 - 13,500 = -$700. The result is negative, so on these figures the service is not a good investment and the company should reconsider.

questions.q: Identify 1 (ONE) BEST technique to assist security and financial analysts in determining if a security control is cost effective to mitigate a vulnerability. [1 Mark]
questions.m: Cost/benefit analysis. Compare the loss the control prevents with what the control costs: value of control = (ALE before control) - (ALE after control) - (annual cost of control). A positive result means the control is worth buying.

questions.q: He is in charge of the data in a certain data domain (data classification). He must guarantee that the information inside that domain is correctly maintained across various platforms and business processes. Identify who has the primary responsibility of determining the classification level for information. [1 Mark]
questions.m: The data owner. The owner classifies the information and decides who may access it; the custodian maintains and protects it at that classification.

questions.q: Explain Threat amplifiers and Threat inhibitors with an example for each. [1 Mark]
questions.m: Threat amplifiers raise the likelihood that an attack is attempted: peer pressure, fame, personal gain, political motives. Example: a hacker group praising an attack encourages copycats. Threat inhibitors lower it: fear of capture, fear of failure, difficulty of the attack, cost of participation, level of sensitivity. Example: strong monitoring makes detection likely, so the attacker chooses another target.

questions.q: Explain Decision Tree Analysis and identify the risk assessment technique that applies to it. [2 Marks]
questions.m: A decision tree maps each decision and its possible outcomes as branches, with the probability and the cost or benefit of each path, so the expected value of each option can be compared and the best one chosen. Each node asks a yes/no question and leads to the next step until an acceptable option is reached. It belongs to risk evaluation: you are evaluating options against whether the resulting risk is acceptable.

questions.q: You are a security officer in company XYZ. Your manager requests you to prepare the asset identification documentation. Write the name of the process/activity of asset identification. [0.5 Marks]
questions.m: Asset identification and inventory: listing every information asset the organization holds before it can be valued, classified and protected. (Asset valuation is the step that follows, once the inventory exists.)

questions.q: List 2 (TWO) information assets with 2 (TWO) attributes of each. [1 Mark]
questions.m: For example: a customer database, with attributes owner (marketing manager) and classification (confidential); and a payroll application server, with attributes IP address/location (data centre rack 4) and asset value (critical). Recognised attributes include name, ID number, owner, classification, location, serial or version number, manufacturer and value.

questions.q: Your company is developing a modern application that will run as an Azure App Service web app. You plan to perform threat modelling to identify potential security issues by using the Microsoft Threat Modelling Tool. Write the name of the threat modelling method and identify 2 (TWO) important requirements needed for the process. [2 Marks]
questions.m: The Microsoft Threat Modelling Tool uses STRIDE (Spoofing, Tampering, Repudiation, Information disclosure, Denial of service, Elevation of privilege). Two requirements for the process: a data flow diagram or architecture of the application showing components, trust boundaries and data flows; and an inventory of the assets and entry points to be protected. The output is a list of threats per component with the controls that address them.

questions.q: Write 1 (ONE) condition when you should apply Risk Avoidance. [1 Mark]
questions.m: Apply avoidance when the risk is so high that no acceptable control can bring it down, and the loss would outweigh the benefit of the activity. You then stop or do not start that activity, or choose an alternative approach that does not carry the risk.

questions.q: Identify 2 (TWO) steps you need to do after finishing the risk assessment task. [2 Marks]
questions.m: After assessment comes risk control (treatment): select and implement the countermeasures for the prioritised risks. Then risk review and monitoring: document and report the results to management, and re-check the risks periodically so new or changed risks are caught. Presenting the ranked findings and recommendations to management is part of that handover.
